title: Telling it your way
job: Retell a known story in your own register
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: passato remoto, THIRD PERSON ONLY and for recognition: fu, ebbe, disse, fece, andò, venne, vide, visse and their plurals
trapassato prossimo, productive: avevo or ero plus an owned participle
condizionale passato with essere: sarei dovuto andare, the twin of L4-M3's avrei dovuto
imperfetto and passato prossimo, L2-M10's and L3-M10's, carrying everything the two above do not

rules.text: THE PASSATO REMOTO IS A READING TENSE, AND THIS MODULE TEACHES IT ONLY TO BE RECOGNISED. Learn the third persons and stop there: fu / furono, ebbe / ebbero, disse / dissero, fece / fecero, andò / andarono, venne / vennero, vide / videro, visse / vissero. That is the whole list you need for a printed story. Do not put yourself in it - no io and no tu form of this tense is taught here, and using one out loud makes you sound like a book read aloud.

THE TRAPASSATO IS THE CHEAPEST TENSE LEFT IN THE COURSE, AND ENGLISH GIVES IT TO YOU FREE. avevo or ero plus a participle: Quando sono arrivato, era partito. Every piece is already yours - avevo and era are L2-M10's, the participles are L3-M10's - and English had already left maps onto it one for one. What is new is only the combination.

ENGLISH MARKS HAD ONCE AND THEN LETS THE PARAGRAPH RUN IN THE SIMPLE PAST. Italian does not: every event that happened before the point you are standing at keeps its trapassato, for as long as you stay standing there. Dropping back into the passato prossimo re-orders the story without meaning to.

SAREI DOVUTO ANDARE IS THE ESSERE HALF OF A FORM YOU HALF OWN. L4-M3 shipped avrei dovuto and avrei potuto, both on avere. When the verb underneath takes essere - andare, partire, venire - the whole thing takes essere too, and the participle agrees: sarei dovuto andare, sarei dovuta andare. It is one cell of a paradigm, not a new tense.

AN ENGLISH RETELLING KEEPS THE SOURCE TENSE AND AN ITALIAN RETELLING CHANGES IT. The same story is remoto on the page and prossimo out loud: disse in print becomes ha detto when you tell it. That swap is the exercise of this module - read the one, say the other, and never mix them inside a single telling.

THE RETELLING KIT IS SIX WORDS AND TWO FRAMES. c'era una volta opens; protagonista and personaggio name who it is about; versione is YOUR telling as against the printed one; in breve and per farla breve cut it short; la morale closes it. fiaba and favola are the same thing, and either can be used of a story with a lesson in it.

sentences.display: C'era una volta una bambina che abitava in un paese piccolo
sentences.cue: Once upon a time there was a girl who lived in a small village
sentences.literal: There was one time a girl who lived in a village small

words.note: Three tokens over two rows you own - L2-M10's c'era and L4-M8's una volta - and learned whole, because it is a formula and not a description of a time.

sentences.trap: The verb after it is an imperfetto, not a remoto: che abitava, not che abitò. The opening is frozen; what follows it is the ordinary past of description.
sentences.sound: che-RA U-na VOL-ta, run as one phrase with no pause inside it.

variations.display: C'era una volta una bambina
variations.cue: Once upon a time there was a girl
variations.changed: the opening with nothing after it

variations.display: C'era una volta un gatto che dormiva sempre
variations.cue: Once upon a time there was a cat who always slept
variations.changed: a different subject in the same frame

mistake.why: The c' is not decoration. c'era is there was; era alone is it was, and the formula loses its there.

sentences.usage: Opening any story anybody already knows - to a child, or as a joke to an adult.
sentences.mnemonic: there was one time - and Italian says it in exactly that order.

sentences.display: In questa fiaba la protagonista era una bambina
sentences.cue: In this fairy tale the main character was a girl
sentences.literal: In this fairy-tale the protagonist was a girl

words.cue: fairy tale, story with a lesson
words.note: fiaba and favola are the same thing and both are used. Either can be the story you retell, and la morale della favola is the fixed phrase for its lesson.
One ending for both genders in the singular: la protagonista and il protagonista. Only the article tells you which, which is unusual and worth noticing.

sentences.trap: protagonista does not change for a woman. il protagonista and la protagonista are the same word, and inventing protagonisto or protagonista-feminine is the reflex to resist.
sentences.sound: FIA-ba, two syllables. pro-ta-go-NIS-ta, stress on NIS.

variations.display: In questa fiaba la protagonista è una bambina
variations.cue: In this fairy tale the main character is a girl
variations.changed: the present, which is how you talk about a story you are holding

variations.display: La protagonista della fiaba era una bambina
variations.cue: The main character of the fairy tale was a girl
variations.changed: the story named after the character instead

mistake.display: In questa fiaba il protagonista era una bambina
mistake.why: The article has to agree even though the noun cannot. With una bambina it must be la protagonista.

sentences.usage: Setting up a retelling: which story, and who it is about.

sentences.display: Il personaggio disse una cosa strana e andò a casa
sentences.cue: The character said something strange and went home
sentences.literal: The character said a thing strange and went to home

words.note: Any character; protagonista is the one the story is about. Of a real person it means a public figure, and it is faintly ironic.
The passato remoto of dire, third person. You will read it constantly and you should never say it: out loud this is ha detto, L3-M5's.
The remoto of andare. The accent on the o is the tense - ando with no accent is nothing at all - and out loud it becomes è andato.

sentences.trap: Read disse, say ha detto. Both are the same event; the printed page uses one tense and a person telling you the story uses the other.
sentences.sound: per-so-NAG-gio. DIS-se, double s. an-DO, all the weight on the accented final o.

variations.display: Il personaggio disse una cosa strana
variations.cue: The character said something strange
variations.changed: the first half alone

variations.display: Andò a casa e non disse niente
variations.cue: He went home and said nothing
variations.changed: the two remoto verbs the other way round

variations.display: Dissero una cosa strana e andarono a casa
variations.cue: They said something strange and went home
variations.changed: both verbs in the plural

mistake.display: Io dissi una cosa strana e andai a casa
mistake.why: The first person of this tense is not taught here and should not be produced. A speaker telling their own story says ho detto and sono andato.

sentences.usage: Reading a printed story, or reporting what one says.
sentences.mnemonic: the accented final vowel is the remoto's signature.

sentences.display: Fu una storia lunga. Visse molti anni in città
sentences.cue: It was a long story. He lived many years in the city
sentences.literal: It was a story long. He lived many years in city

words.note: The remoto of essere. Short, irregular and everywhere in print; out loud the same sentence is è stata, L3-M10's.
The remoto of vivere. It is the form a fairy tale ends on - e vissero felici - and it is the one line of remoto most learners already half know.

sentences.trap: fu has no accent and is not a shortened form of anything. It is the whole word, and it is not furono's singular by dropping letters.
sentences.sound: FU, one syllable and no accent. VIS-se, double s held.

variations.display: Fu una storia lunga
variations.cue: It was a long story
variations.changed: the judgement alone

variations.display: Visse molti anni in città
variations.cue: He lived many years in the city
variations.changed: the life alone

variations.display: Furono anni difficili. Vissero in città
variations.cue: They were difficult years. They lived in the city
variations.changed: both verbs in the plural

mistake.why: fui is the first person - I was - and a story is not you. The third person is fu, and it is the only person of this tense the module asks for.

sentences.usage: Reading, and recognising the two commonest remoto verbs on the page.
sentences.mnemonic: fu and visse: the two you will meet first.

sentences.display: Quando sono arrivato, era partito da un'ora
sentences.cue: When I arrived, he had left an hour before
sentences.literal: When I am arrived, he was left from an hour

words.note: The trapassato: L2-M10's era plus L3-M10's participle. Two owned words, one new tense, and it maps straight onto English had left.

sentences.trap: Not sono arrivato e lui è partito. That puts the two events side by side; the trapassato is what says one of them was already over when the other happened.
sentences.sound: E-ra par-TI-to, four syllables and no pause between the two words.

variations.display: Quando sono arrivato, era già partito
variations.cue: When I arrived, he had already left
variations.changed: L4-M6's già dropped in, where English also puts already

variations.display: Era partito da un'ora
variations.cue: He had left an hour before
variations.changed: the earlier event on its own

mistake.why: The passato prossimo makes him leave AFTER you arrived. The whole point of the sentence is that he was gone already, and only the trapassato says so.

sentences.usage: Retelling anything, because a retelling always reorders what happened.

sentences.display: Avevo finito il lavoro quando è arrivata mia madre
sentences.cue: I had finished the work when my mother arrived
sentences.literal: I had finished the work when is arrived my mother

words.note: The avere half of the same tense. finito is L3-M10's participle and avevo is L2-M10's imperfetto; nothing here is new except the pair.

sentences.trap: With avere the participle does not agree: avevo finito whoever is speaking. The agreement in era partita belongs to essere, not to the tense.
sentences.sound: a-VE-vo fi-NI-to, five syllables, both stresses in the middle.

variations.display: Avevo finito il lavoro
variations.cue: I had finished the work
variations.changed: the earlier event alone

variations.display: Quando è arrivata mia madre, avevo finito
variations.cue: When my mother arrived, I had finished
variations.changed: the two halves swapped, which Italian allows

mistake.display: Ho finito il lavoro quando è arrivata mia madre
mistake.why: That says you finished AT the moment she arrived. avevo finito is what puts the finishing before her arrival, which is what the sentence means.

sentences.usage: Any account where the order of events is the point.
sentences.mnemonic: avevo + participle, and no agreement to worry about.

sentences.display: Sarei dovuto andare prima. Alla fine sono rimasto
sentences.cue: I should have gone earlier. In the end I stayed
sentences.literal: I would-be had-to to-go earlier. At the end I am stayed

words.note: The essere twin of L4-M3's avrei dovuto. andare takes essere, so the whole compound does, and the participle dovuto agrees with the speaker.

sentences.trap: Not avrei dovuto andare. The auxiliary is chosen by the verb at the END - andare - and not by dovere, which is why this cell needs saying at all.
sentences.sound: sa-REI do-VU-to an-DA-re, six syllables run together as one idea.

variations.display: Sarei dovuto andare prima
variations.cue: I should have gone earlier
variations.changed: the regret without the outcome

variations.display: Alla fine sono rimasto
variations.cue: In the end I stayed
variations.changed: the outcome without the regret

variations.display: Sarei dovuta andare prima
variations.cue: I should have gone earlier
variations.changed: a woman speaking, so the participle agrees

mistake.why: Heard, and taught in some books, but this course takes the essere line: with an essere verb underneath, the compound goes to essere and the participle agrees.

sentences.usage: Looking back at a decision inside a story you are telling about yourself.
sentences.mnemonic: the last verb picks the auxiliary.

sentences.display: In breve, la morale della favola è questa
sentences.cue: In short, the moral of the story is this
sentences.literal: In brief, the moral of the fable is this

words.note: The cut. It warns the listener that you are about to skip most of it, which is exactly what a retelling does.
Feminine here - la morale della favola. The same spelling as the adjective moral, and only the article separates them.

sentences.trap: la morale is the lesson; il morale is somebody's spirits. Same five letters, different article, opposite conversations.
sentences.sound: in BRE-ve. mo-RA-le, stress on RA.

variations.display: In breve, la morale è questa
variations.cue: In short, the moral is this
variations.changed: the story left unnamed

variations.display: La morale della favola è questa
variations.cue: The moral of the story is this
variations.changed: the closing without the warning

mistake.display: In breve, il morale della favola è questa
mistake.why: il morale is morale in the sense of spirits. The lesson of a story is la morale, and the article is the only thing carrying that.

sentences.usage: Closing a retelling, or cutting one short when you can see it is going long.
sentences.mnemonic: LA morale teaches; IL morale needs cheering up.

sentences.display: Per farla breve, questa versione è la mia
sentences.cue: To cut a long story short, this version is mine
sentences.literal: For to-make-it short, this version is the mine

words.cue: to cut a long story short
words.note: Three tokens, learned whole, with a clitic la inside it that stands for the story - exactly the machine L5-M8 took apart.
The word that makes your retelling yours: la mia versione is not a claim that the printed one is wrong, only that this one is how you tell it.

sentences.trap: per farla breve is fixed. The la inside it refers to nothing you can name, and swapping it for lo or for a noun breaks the phrase.
sentences.sound: per FAR-la BRE-ve. ver-SIO-ne, stress on SIO.

variations.display: Per farla breve, questa è la mia versione
variations.cue: To cut a long story short, this is my version
variations.changed: the possessive moved after the noun's article

variations.display: Questa versione è la mia
variations.cue: This version is mine
variations.changed: the claim without the warning

mistake.display: Per farlo breve, questa versione è la mia
mistake.why: The clitic is la and does not agree with anything in your sentence. It is frozen inside the phrase, and farlo breve is simply not the expression.

sentences.usage: Warning somebody that what follows is the short telling, and yours.
sentences.mnemonic: farla breve: the la is the story, and it never changes.

sentences.display: Ebbe paura, vide il mare, fece una cosa strana e venne a casa
sentences.cue: He was afraid, saw the sea, did something strange and came home
sentences.literal: He had fear, saw the sea, did a thing strange and came to home

words.note: The remoto of avere. ebbe paura is was afraid, on L2-M9's ha paura - the noun does not change, only the tense under it.
The remoto of vedere. Out loud it is ha visto, L3-M5's, and the two look nothing like each other, which is why this one has to be recognised rather than derived.
The remoto of fare. ha fatto out loud. Like fu and disse it is short and irregular, and there is no rule to reach for.
The remoto of venire. Not to be read as a form of volere: è venuto is what the same event becomes in speech.

sentences.trap: Four verbs, four irregular stems, and no pattern joining them. This tense is learned as a list of shapes to recognise, and pretending it is regular is what makes it unreadable.
sentences.sound: EB-be. VI-de. FE-ce. VEN-ne. Every one has its stress on the first syllable.

variations.display: Ebbe paura e non disse niente
variations.cue: He was afraid and said nothing
variations.changed: two of the four, in a shorter line

variations.display: Vide il mare e venne a casa
variations.cue: He saw the sea and came home
variations.changed: the other two

variations.display: Fece una cosa strana e venne a casa
variations.cue: He did something strange and came home
variations.changed: the same events with fare in front

mistake.display: Ebbi paura, vidi il mare e venni a casa
mistake.why: Those are the first persons, and they are not this module's. Telling your own story out loud, the line is ho avuto paura, ho visto il mare, sono venuto a casa.

sentences.usage: Reading a page of a story, and recognising the four verbs that carry most of it.
sentences.mnemonic: ebbe, vide, fece, venne: four shapes, no rule.
